Half of Bristol's tap water comes from a canal 💧
Bristol Water says that in drier weather just over half comes from the Gloucester and Sharpness Canal, mostly fed by the River Severn. More than a third comes from four Mendip reservoirs (Chew Valley, Blagdon, Cheddar, Barrow) holding about 38 billion litres, and about a tenth from springs, wells and boreholes. On 4 November the reservoirs were 43% full, up from 35% a year earlier.
